subject: Ingress safety net and product decisions for AsterHealth launch
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Shaw <elliot@asterhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ingress safety net and product decisions for AsterHealth launch

Team —

AsterHealth is ready to go-live next week (Wed 5/27). They just confirmed an initial ramp that could peak for a 3-hour window if their marketing test goes viral. Key asks from them and from Sales:

- Temporary throughput increase for the 3-hour spike window (estimate attached)
- Clear fallback policy if latency or errors climb (they prefer degraded model rather than 5xx)
- Product toggles for features that increase token usage (summarization + metadata enrichment)

Please see the attached traffic model (Aster_Launch_Traffic_v2.xlsx) — Marissa, you own the numbers. David, I need an ops-safe plan that avoids a full outage but lets the customer proceed. Priya, product needs to sign off on the toggles and what we can reasonably degrade.

Concrete asks:
1) Short-term quota bump: how much can we safely give for a 48-hour window?
2) Fallback behavior: can we route to a smaller quantized variant (rw-small-q4) under load and automatically throttle enrichment features?
3) Canary approach: what metrics and thresholds do we require before full rollout?

I'll be looping Elliot and Kaylee from Aster so they know the guardrails. Reply with runbook suggestions and any product constraints.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Sales Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Shaw <elliot@asterhealth.com>, Kaylee Ortiz <kaylee@asterhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress safety net and product decisions for AsterHealth launch

Mina —

Thanks for the heads-up. Aster confirmed the attached ramp (tab:peak_scenarios). Quick summary:
- Baseline: ~85 tpm, ~1.2k tokens / request average
- Expected peak window (test): 3 hours with spikes up to ~420 tpm (approximately 5x baseline)
- Estimated sustained increase after test (if successful): +30% week-over-week for first 2 weeks

Requested temporary entitlements: +5x burst allowance for a 3-hour block on Wed 5/27 (UTC: 16:00-19:00). We'd like auto-fallback to a smaller model (rw-medium-q4) if p95 latency exceeds 1.2s or error rate >1.5%. We also propose disabling metadata enrichment during the peak to shave ~35% of token usage.

Open product questions for Priya: is dynamic enrichment toggle feasible at runtime per-customer? If not, we need a manual feature-flag and a rollback plan.

Ops — happy to adjust numbers if you need more headroom.

—Marissa
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: Aster_Launch_Traffic_v2.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Elliot Shaw <elliot@asterhealth.com>
Date: Sat, 23 May 2026 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress safety net and product decisions for AsterHealth launch

Thanks Marissa — useful detail. Ops constraints and suggestions:

- Short answer on quota bump: we can provision a temporary 4x burst reserve for the 3-hour window with 2-hour warmup. 5x is risky without guaranteed pre-warm.
- Fallback model: rw-medium-q4 -> rw-small-q4 is supported; switching is ~30s for new sessions but we need to drain long-lived sessions gracefully.
- Token-saving levers: disabling enrichment is the biggest win; also reduce generation max_tokens by 20% during the window.
- Recommended safety net: staged canary (5% -> 25% -> 100% over 90 minutes) with automatic rollback on p95 >1.0s OR error rate >1.0%.
- Throttles: implement per-customer ingress rate cap at 2x baseline for first 30 minutes after go-live, then allow controlled increases per canary stage.

Telemetry & preflight asks (need answers):
1) What percentage of Aster requests are chat/generation vs embeddings? (embeddings are cheaper but heavy throughput)
2) Are there long-poll websocket sessions that keep KV cache warm?

If you confirm percentages, we can calculate required GPU slots and provide an exact delta. For now I'll provision a 4x burst on standby and mark the change as manual to avoid accidental use.

-David
David Kim
Infrastructure & Reliability
david_kim@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Shaw <elliot@asterhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress safety net and product decisions for AsterHealth launch

Quick product clarifications:

- Dynamic enrichment toggle: yes, feature-flaggable per-customer, but we need a 24-hour lead to push the flag and validate metrics recording. We cannot do an instantaneous toggle without QA.
- Degraded model behavior: we support automatic fallback to rw-medium-q4 with reduced max_tokens. Fallback to rw-small-q4 is allowed but requires explicit rollout approval (quality might drop noticeably).
- Telemetry hooks: require the following be present in client calls for canary evaluation: request_id, session_id, model_version, enrichment_flag. If Aster cannot instrument request_id/session_id we will lose canary fidelity.

I've uploaded a short canary playbook to the team drive (see link). I recommend the staged canary David proposed, with the first stage limited to non-critical customer segments (internal testers + 5% traffic). Also, product will default to disabling enrichment if p95 >1.0s during the peak window.

Priya
Director, Product Management
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Attachment: canary_playbook.md (text/markdown)
Link: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/AsterHealth+Launch

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elliot Shaw <elliot@asterhealth.com>, Kaylee Ortiz <kaylee@asterhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ingress safety net and product decisions for AsterHealth launch

All — great alignment. Summary and next steps (action owners):

1) Entitlement: Ops (David) will provision a manual 4x burst reserve for Wed 5/27 16:00-19:00 UTC. If the 2-hour warmup completes successfully, David will consider on-the-fly increase to 5x but only with confirmation from Marissa and Priya. (owner: David)
2) Canary: staged rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 90 minutes with automatic rollback triggers p95 >1.0s OR error rate >1.0%. (owner: Priya + David)
3) Product toggles: Priya to schedule the enrichment feature-flag push by Tues 5/26 EOD; Marissa to confirm Aster can accept enrichment off during peak. (owner: Priya, Marissa)
4) Fallback model: default fallback to rw-medium-q4; fallback to rw-small-q4 requires explicit approval after quality check. (owner: Product)
5) Telemetry: Marissa to confirm Aster will surface request_id and session_id by Mon 5/25 noon. If not present, canary fidelity drops and we will keep conservative caps. (owner: Marissa)

Elliot/Kaylee — we will follow up with a short runbook and a timeboxed decision call Tuesday 5/26 at 13:00 PT. Expect a runbook link and the temp entitlement confirmation by EOD Mon.

Thanks everyone —
Mina
Sales Ops Lead, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com
